notes.text: The page defines the special oriented topological Teichmüller groupoid from pairs (X,S), with X a compact oriented surface with boundary and S a finite subset of its boundary, and isotopy classes of isomorphisms as morphisms. The S-empty subcase receives T-top notation. A plus/minus variant permits homeomorphisms without necessarily preserving orientation and is accompanied by a sign/signature functor and a fibre statement. These source definitions and assertions are transcribed, not established by transcription.

The second construction uses (X,Sigma,S), with Sigma a compact one-dimensional submanifold of the interior and S finite in Sigma union boundary X. The old closedness word fermée is cancelled in favor of compactness. The notation is visibly revised from an S-like letter to D, and the raised dévissage replaces the cancelled quoted sauvage candidate. The NB identifies the Sigma-empty objects by a vertical equality and writes an open-immersion replacement over the cancelled full-immersion phrase. The final item writes T S-top plus/minus even though D was used in the preceding notation; the source S and the missing/added S-prefix variations are preserved, not repaired.

Conditional qualification of the sign-functor/fibre assertion: if disconnected X with independent orientation reversal on components is allowed, take S empty and X the disjoint union of two oriented disks. The identity and the two independent component reflections generate C2×C2; only the identity in this subgroup preserves both component orientations. Restricting a functor to the one-object groupoid [±1] gives a homomorphism C2×C2 to C2, whose kernel cannot be trivial because four elements map into two. Thus the asserted orientation-preserving fibre needs connectedness or a uniform-sign convention. This is conditional on that disconnected interpretation and is not a fault asserted against an unstated connectedness convention. The source definition is unchanged.

The first category enclosure is open at the top; the variant enclosure has a top stroke but an open upper-right join. Both are drawn as seen. The unknown cancelled target and the isolated crossed mark are reproduced in small doubtful TikZ drawings, without supplying a mathematical identity or a numeral. The literal point after de and the later unmatched closing parenthesis are retained. The signature caption has an opening parenthesis only.

The uniformly pale nested contours and small circles under the lower dark writing, with brown bleed-like dots and no corresponding dark graph or labels on this face, are treated as show-through background. C incorrectly promotes them into a separate recto figure. No exact verso or other-leaf match was checked, and none is claimed. The complete lower-block blind audit includes this region so the classification can be assessed independently. The folio is 70 with attribution left uncertain.

Physical reading count is 37 text/formula runs, including separately positioned caption, interlinear replacement and cancelled lines, the vertical-equality annotation and the folio. The isolated unidentified mark is additionally covered as a drawing. All 16 first-reader crops were viewed. The complete lower block is one audit unit to avoid repeating its revision and background regions across separate rectangles.
